domain: distributed systems / correlation-ID propagation (session identity across process forks, resume, and compaction boundaries)
axioms: An identity token is only as good as the last boundary that refreshed it; if a lifecycle transition doesn't rewrite it, the token silently outlives its referent
A precedence rule between registers encodes a bet about which one updates first on any given transition, and the bet can be wrong on transitions the design didn't enumerate
Two processes that both lose all signal collapse to the same fallback value and become indistinguishable, regardless of how many registers feed the chain
Environment-variable inheritance is boundary-specific (exec vs spawn vs tool-managed-env) and cannot be assumed uniform across a codebase's call sites
A cross-runtime handoff (e.g. a Claude subprocess launched under a Codex parent) can leave foreign registers set in the child's environment purely by inheritance, not by intent
failure_mode: does not have visibility into the actual Claude Code runtime internals -- claims about resume/compaction behavior are inferential, not verified against the binary
may over-index on distributed-tracing analogies that don't map cleanly onto a single-machine CLI tool's process model
not positioned to judge the git/hash mechanics of the rig check or the evadability of the structural grep pattern
